text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Coles Myer annual report yesterday revealed chief executive Peter Bartels as Australia's highest paid executive, with a A$2.8 million salary package, increased by more than A$1 million in the year to July 28. The report also showed that 180 of the company's directors and executives were paid a total of A$47.89 million. Page 1.

A recent share slump of Internet stocks has seen the share prices of Australia's four Internet stocks, Sausage Software, Solution 6, Netcomm and OzEmail, fall by between 16 and 26 percent over the past two weeks. The CBOE Internet Index, which tracks 15 leading U.S. Internet stocks, has also declined 22 percent in the year to date. Page 1.

The Foreign Investment Review Board last night rejected moves to give Optus Communications' foreign shareholders new voting rights once the company is floated. Treasurer Peter Costello said the move would have significantly increased the influence of the two core telecommunication companies, U.S.-based BellSouth and the UK-based Cable and Wireless CWL.L. Page 3.

Forming part of Colonial Investment Management's plans to boost the value of funds under management globally from almost A$18 billion to A$20 billion by late 1998, CIM managing director Peter Polson confirmed yesterday that the company was set to establish a A$500 million asset management joint venture in South-East Asia. Page 25.

Hazelton Airlines Ltd founder Max Hazelton confirmed yesterday he would join 19.9 percent shareholder Skippers Aviation in backing Sir Brian Massy-Greene as chairman at the annual general meeting on Friday, until a replacement chairman could be secured. Hazelton also said the company would be in "grave danger" of a takeover bid once it returned to profitability. Page 25.

ING Group chairman Aad Jacobs said yesterday the giant Dutch bancassurance conglomerate was very happy with the performance of its Australian businesses and was on the lookout for more acquisitions in Australia to boost its fully-owned subsidiary, Mercantile Mutual Holdings. Page 26.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following the release of Coles Myer Ltd's annual report yesterday, the troubled retailer's chief executive Peter Bartels was unveiled as possibly the nation's highest paid chief executive officer on a salary of A$2.87 million, up from A$1.63 million. Anticipating criticism, Coles said executive directors had benefited from bonus payments tied to the company's 1995 results. Page 21.

With former Coles Myer Ltd chairman Solomon Lew's re-election as a director now seemingly assured, the level of dealings between Coles and Lew has declined for the first time since related party transactions were itemised in the annual report. Toy, clothing, housewares and other interests associated with Lew sold A$100.8 million of goods to Coles last year, down from A$104.5 million in 1995. Page 21.

Amidst recent confusion about the extent of disclosure required, the Companies and Securities Advisory Committee will soon finish a review of the continuous disclosure provision contained in the Corporations Law and Australian Stock Exchange listing rules. Rather than recommending a wholesale overhaul of the rules, it is expected to suggest some changes. Page 21.

In a bid to increase efficiency at its Mt Isa operations, MIM Holdings Ltd yesterday announced plans to sell 80 percent of its Mica Creek power station to Queensland Government generator AUSTA Electric, naming AUSTA as its preferred independent power proucer to operate and oversee a A$100 million expansion and conversion from coal to gas next year of the Mica Creek plant. Page 23.

Ignoring pressure from institutional shareholders to hold a shareholder meeting to approve its A$2.6 billion takeover of Advance Bank, St George Bank Ltd said last night it was seeking a determination on the question from the listing committee of the Australian Stock Exchange. Page 23.

Contrary to a press report yesterday that ANZ Banking Group Ltd was considering a A$24 billion alliance with the UK's Standard Chartered Bank, using a similar structure to the RTZ-CRA merger, ANZ released a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange saying it wa not investigating or discussing a merger with Standard Chartered. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Releasing its annual report yesterday, Coles Myer revealed that its largest shareholder, Solomon Lew, received more than A$100 million from business dealings with the retailer in 1995/96 and managing director and chief executive Peter Bartels was paid beteen A$2.87 million and A$2.88 million. Coles also said Melbourne corporate lawyer Peter Willcocks was seeking a seat on the company's board. Page 25.

Awaiting a clearance from authorities on the disclosure requirements for the Seven legal action, Optus Communications and major shareholder Mayne Nickless are expected to lodge a revamped float proposal with the Australian Securities Commission in the next two weeks. The planned 1996 float of Optus Communications was jeopardised when Seven Network launched legal action against its pay TV offshoot Optus Vision almost three weeks ago. Page 25.

The Australian Securities Commission has launched a A$210 million claim against Permanent Trustee and its parent and guarantor, Permanent Trustee Co, on behalf of 23,000 unitholders in the Aust-Wide property trusts. Mounted under section 50 of the Corportions Law, the case could set a milestone for investors who have lost money in a public vehicle and cannot afford to launch their own legal action. Page 25.

St George Bank is seeking an exemption from the Australian Stock Exchange to avoid holding a shareholders meeting to vote on its A$2.65 billion proposed takeover of Advance Bank. Although St George said it still might hold a shareholders' meeting, it is een to avoid giving its major shareholder, National Australia Bank, the opportunity to oppose the merger. Page 27.

Australian National Industries yesterday announced the terms of reference for a full investigation into the controversial acquisition of German environmental engineering group ABT from Kerry Packer's Consolidated Press in 1991. ANI has appointed prominen QC Bob Ellicott to examine the purchase. Page 27.

A float of the Ten Group could be close with growing support for a float vehicle linked to Telecasters North Queensland, which has a 40 percent voting interest and 20 percent economic interest in Ten. The proposal has yet to be rejected by Izzy Asper's CanWest Global Communications CWW.TO, which is thought to be generally opposed to any float. Page 27.
THE AGE

In its annual report, retailer Coles Myer revealed managing director and chief executive Peter Bartels was paid between A$2.87 million and A$2.88 million in the year and major shareholder Solomon Lew recieved more than A$100 million from business dealings with Coles in 1995/96. Page C1.

Facing the threat of widespread industrial action unless it comes to an agreement with unions on redundancies and staff reductions, ANZ Bank yesterday furiously denied a newspaper report which said the bank was negotiating a A$24 billion merger with Britih-based Standard Chartered banking group and had engaged Goldman Sachs and Swiss Bank Corporation to structure the deal. Page C1.

As part of a A$210 million damages claim launched by the Australian Securities Commission on behalf of 23,000 unit holders, the New South Wales Supreme Court heard yesterday that between 1988 and 1990 Aust-Wide Trust and Australia Wide Flexi Property Fund engaged in unauthorised investments by investing unit-holder money into units in the Northbourne Securities Property Trust. Page C1.

Sunraysia Television chairman Eva Presser bought 80,000 Sunraysia shares last week to lift her beneficial shareholding to 49.65 percent, in a move which strengthens her control over the company, which operates Perth's Channel Nine, and makes it a more dificult target for takeover bids. Page C3.

UK retailer Marks & Spencer's plans to send a country manager to Australia in the first quarter of 1997 to begin looking for a franchise partner that would open and operate all M & S stores in Australia, making Australia one of the company' top Asia-Pacific franchises. Page C3.

After reporting a 17.4 percent increase in first-quarter profit to A$1.22 million and a 2.3 percent increase in sales to A$15.67 million, Blackmores managing director Marcus Blackmore said the health products group would use advertising as its key stratgy in overcoming flat retail sales. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
